# AES Module Design Specification

## 1. Overview

The module is a memory-mapped AES cryptographic accelerator peripheral. It provides AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 encryption and decryption of 128-bit data blocks. It supports ECB, CBC, CFB-128, OFB, and CTR cipher modes.

The module is controlled by software through a TL-UL register interface. It also provides an idle indication, a key sideload input, an entropy distribution interface, alert outputs, and a life-cycle escalation input.

The module shall be configurable at build time to enable or disable optional functionality such as AES-192 support and side-channel countermeasures.

## 2. Build-Time Configuration

The module behavior may be configured with the following build-time options:

- AES-192 support may be enabled or disabled. When disabled, the module shall not perform AES-192 operations.
- First-order masking of the cipher core may be enabled or disabled.
- When masking is enabled, the masked S-Box implementation may be selected.
- A delay may be configured between a software start trigger and the actual start of an AES operation.
- The ability to force mask randomness to zero may be allowed or disallowed.
- Entropy reseeding requests may be skipped entirely.
- Alert synchronization behavior may be selected per alert.
- The initialization constants used by internal pseudo-random generators may be configured.

These options are constant during operation and do not change the programming model except as described in later sections.

## 3. Reset and Initialization

On reset, the module shall perform an initialization sequence before becoming operational. During this sequence:

- Any internal pseudo-random generators required for clearing and masking shall be reseeded.
- Key, initialization vector, and data registers shall be overwritten with pseudo-random data.
- The module shall not indicate idle until this initialization sequence is complete.
- If entropy reseeding is disabled by configuration, the module shall initialize using its built-in random state and shall not wait for external entropy.

After initialization, the values in key, IV, and data registers shall not be assumed to have reset-defined values.

The module shall also support a separate reset input for shadowed configuration state. Such state shall be reset independently of the main reset.

## 4. Register Interface

The module shall act as a TL-UL slave peripheral. It shall accept read and write transactions and update its register state accordingly.

The module shall provide:

- Configuration and control registers.
- Status registers.
- Write-only key registers.
- Write-only input data registers.
- Read-only output data registers.
- Initialization vector registers.
- Trigger registers for starting operations, clearing registers, and requesting reseeding.
- Alert test registers.

All multi-word values shall be little-endian unless explicitly noted otherwise.

The configuration register shall be shadowed. A configuration change shall take effect only after software performs two write operations to the configuration register.

Writes to the configuration register, key registers, and IV registers shall be ignored while the module is not idle.

Key registers shall not be readable.

Software-triggered operations such as starting an AES operation, clearing registers, and requesting entropy reseeding shall be initiated by writing to the trigger interface. The start trigger shall be automatically cleared once the requested AES operation begins.

## 5. AES Operation

### 5.1 Operation Modes

The module shall support:

- AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256, subject to build-time configuration.
- Encryption and decryption.
- ECB, CBC, CFB-128, OFB, and CTR modes.

Only one operation shall be performed at a time. When the module is busy with an AES operation, writes to configuration, key, and IV registers shall be ignored.

### 5.2 Automatic and Manual Operation

The module shall support automatic and manual operation modes.

In automatic operation mode:

- The module shall automatically start encryption or decryption when a complete input data block is available.
- The module shall not overwrite unread output data.
- If the previous output data block has not been fully read, the module shall stall and shall not begin processing the next block until all required output registers have been read.

In manual operation mode:

- The module shall start an AES operation only when software writes the start trigger.
- The module shall start even if the IV or input data registers have not been fully updated.
- The module shall not provide output back-pressure. New output data may overwrite previous output data regardless of whether it has been read.

If a start delay is configured, the module shall wait for the configured number of cycles after the start trigger before beginning the AES operation.

### 5.3 Key and IV Requirements

Before starting an AES operation, the following conditions shall be met:

- The configuration shall have been written.
- A valid key shall be available.
- In CBC, CFB, OFB, or CTR mode, the IV shall be ready.

The module shall consider the IV ready if all IV registers have been written at least once since the last IV update, or if none of them have been changed. A partially updated IV shall not be considered ready.

In ECB mode, IV values are ignored.

### 5.4 Initial Key Handling

The key may be provided in one of two ways:

- Through the key registers.
- Through the key sideload interface.

When the key is provided through the key registers, the actual key shall be the XOR combination of the two key shares written to the key register banks. All required key registers for the selected AES key length must be written at least once. The order of writes does not matter.

When key sideload is enabled:

- Writes to the key registers shall be ignored.
- The module shall use the key supplied on the key sideload interface.
- The module shall not expose the sideloaded key through the register interface.
- An AES operation shall not start unless the sideloaded key is marked valid.

The module shall not begin an operation with an invalid or incomplete key.

### 5.5 Key Expansion Behavior

The module shall generate round keys internally from the initial key.

When a new key is provided and the next operation is ECB or CBC decryption, the module shall first perform the key expansion needed to derive the final-round decryption key. During this phase, the AES data path shall remain idle. After this phase, decryption with the new key can proceed.

No such initial delay is required for encryption, or for CFB, OFB, or CTR modes.

### 5.6 Data Input and Output

The module shall accept a 128-bit input data block through four write-only data input registers. All four registers must be written at least once for the block to be considered available. The order of writes does not matter.

While the module is processing a data block, software may write the next input data block. The module shall indicate when it is ready to accept the next input block.

When output data is available, the module shall indicate that the output is valid. Output data shall be read from four read-only output data registers. In automatic mode, all four output registers must be read at least once before the module proceeds.

### 5.7 Cipher Mode Behavior

The module shall implement the selected cipher mode as follows:

- ECB: Each data block is encrypted or decrypted independently.
- CBC: The previous ciphertext block is chained into the current block. The IV provides the initial chaining value. The module shall update the IV as required after each block.
- CFB-128: The segment size is fixed to 128 bits. The module shall use the AES encryption of the IV or previous ciphertext to combine with the data block and shall update the chaining value accordingly.
- OFB: The module shall generate keystream blocks by repeatedly encrypting the previous IV and shall update the IV with each generated keystream block.
- CTR: The module shall treat the IV as an initial 128-bit counter value and shall increment it using the standard big-endian incrementing function. The counter value shall be updated after each block.

In CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, the IV registers may be updated by the module during operation. Software shall wait until the module is idle before writing a new IV for a new message.

## 6. Entropy Interface

The module shall request entropy from the entropy distribution interface for reseeding its internal pseudo-random generators.

The module shall support entropy consumers for two purposes:

- Clearing registers with pseudo-random data.
- Masking randomness for the masked cipher core.

When an internal consumer needs entropy, the module shall assert an entropy request. When entropy is supplied, the module shall accept it and route it to the requesting consumer.

The module shall service one entropy response at a time. If multiple consumers request entropy simultaneously, one shall be serviced first and the other shall wait or be serviced in a subsequent cycle.

Reseeding shall be triggered:

- As part of reset initialization.
- When a new key is provided, if enabled by configuration.
- Periodically according to the configured reseed rate.
- When software explicitly requests a reseed.

If reseeding is disabled by configuration, the module shall not issue entropy requests for reseeding and shall operate using its current random state.

If a fatal alert or life-cycle escalation condition is active, a pending entropy request may be dropped before it is acknowledged. The module shall be reset before normal operation resumes.

## 7. Alerts and Life-Cycle Escalation

The module shall provide alert outputs for security-relevant events.

The module shall assert a recoverable alert when a recoverable error is detected in the control configuration update path.

The module shall assert a fatal alert when a fatal integrity or control-flow error is detected.

The module shall provide alert test functionality so software can verify the alert outputs.

When a fatal alert is asserted, the module shall cease processing further data and shall require a reset before becoming operational again.

When life-cycle escalation is asserted:

- The module shall cease normal operation.
- Internal controllers shall enter a terminal error state.
- The module shall not resume operation until reset.
- Pending entropy requests may be dropped.

## 8. Idle Indication

The module shall provide an idle indication output for use by the clock manager.

The idle indication shall be asserted when:

- No AES operation is in progress.
- No initialization or register-clearing sequence is pending.
- The module is ready to accept new software commands.

The idle indication shall not be asserted while the module is busy processing data or waiting on an internal security operation that prevents the module from being safely halted.

## 9. Summary of Programming Constraints

To ensure correct operation:

- Software shall wait for the module to be idle before changing configuration, key, or IV values.
- Software shall write all required key and IV registers.
- Software shall write all four input data registers for each block.
- In automatic mode, software shall read all four output data registers.
- Software shall wait for the start trigger to clear after starting an operation in manual mode.
- Software shall not expect key material to be readable through the register interface.
- After reset, software shall wait for the initialization sequence to complete before relying on the module state.
